name: SiMTraM (Simulation of Mixed Traffic Mobility)
maintainer: Transportation Systems Engineering lab, IIT Bombay (Tom V. Mathew, Caleb Ronald Munigety, Ashutosh Bajpai); SourceForge user 'simtram'
last_activity: Software: 2013-04-29 (SiMTraM-0.1.1-winbin.zip). Paper: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering, 2015 (DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)CP.1943-5487.0000378)
licence: GPLv3 (as declared on the SourceForge project page)
language: C, C++, Python (SourceForge metadata); inherits SUMO's C++ code base of about 2012-2013 (exact SUMO base version not stated) [uncertain]
code_availability: Windows binary only found: SiMTraM-0.1.1-winbin.zip (6.5 MB) on https://sourceforge.net/projects/simtram/. No source archive or SVN/Git repository is visible on the project pages, despite the GPLv3 label and the Linux claim [uncertain]
maintenance_health: Abandoned. No release since April 2013 (13+ years). Zero recent downloads (about 1,899 all-time), no reviews, no issue tracker activity. The SUMO fork base is many major versions behind the current 1.28.0, so forward-porting would mean re-implementation, not merging
car_following: SUMO's (Krauss-type) car-following, modified so that leader identification works across strips (any vehicle overlapping the follower's strips ahead counts as leader) and safe velocity uses vehicle-type-dependent following behaviour [uncertain]
lane_model: Each lane is divided into strips of configurable width. A vehicle occupies as many contiguous strips as its width requires and moves along them. Lateral movement is 'discrete gradual lane changing': strip-by-strip shifts, with a strip-change parameter (lambda) calibrated on the observed number of strip changes. When strip width equals lane width, the model reduces to ordinary lane-based SUMO
lateral_model_type: Strip-based (discretised lateral positions, conceptually close to SUMO's later sublane model)
junction_model: The strip concept was extended to movement at and within intersections, so vehicles keep strip positions through the junction. The exact conflict and priority resolution beyond SUMO's base junction logic is not described in the accessible abstracts [uncertain]
signal_control_modes: Inherited from the SUMO base of 2013 (fixed-time and basic actuated) [uncertain]
flyover_support: Inherited from SUMO (grade separation through non-shared nodes); not a focus of SiMTraM [uncertain]
grade_separation_handling: Not addressed by SiMTraM; inherits 2013-era netconvert behaviour [uncertain]
vehicle_types: Heterogeneous mix with type-dependent width (strip occupancy) and following behaviour, typical of Indian traffic (two-wheelers, three-wheelers, cars, buses, trucks) [uncertain]
gridlock_policy: Inherits SUMO's teleport-on-wait (time-to-teleport) of its 2013 base version; nothing SiMTraM-specific documented [uncertain]
mixed_traffic_support: Yes, the central purpose: homogeneous and heterogeneous traffic, a mix of vehicle types, vehicles not restricted to lanes (SourceForge feature list)
non_lane_behaviour: Supported through strips: vehicles position laterally at strip granularity, and narrower strips give near-continuous lateral movement. Tests showed throughput rises as strip width falls, and strip width equal to lane width matched the lane-based model, a useful sanity check. Lane markings remain the outer frame of the road, so this is lane-free within a carriageway rather than free 2D
seepage_filtering_support: Implicitly possible: narrow vehicles occupying fewer strips can pass alongside wider ones within the same lane. Explicit queue-filtering validation not found [uncertain]
per_class_parameters: Calibrated per-class values are in the 2015 paper, not on the open web; values not retrieved [uncertain]
indian_calibration_evidence: Calibrated and validated with video data from the Eastern Express Highway, Mumbai. The authors report 'close agreement' with real-world data and a better representation of mixed traffic than lane-based modelling. Quantitative error figures not retrieved [uncertain]
calibration_dataset_used: Video-based trajectory or count data, Eastern Express Highway, Mumbai; not published as an open dataset [uncertain]
calibration_method: Strip-change parameter lambda calibrated against the observed number of strip changes; other parameters and the error metric not retrieved [uncertain]
validation_against_field_case: Eastern Express Highway, Mumbai (midblock); intersection validation unclear [uncertain]
network_import: Inherits SUMO 2013-era netconvert (OSM and others); no SiMTraM-specific import [uncertain]
demand_input_formats: SUMO XML routes and flows of its base version [uncertain]
wasm_or_streaming_feasibility: Not practical: binary-only, outdated build chain, no maintained API surface. It would have to run as a server binary under Wine or Windows
api: Presumably the TraCI of its SUMO base version (2013 protocol, incompatible with current clients) [uncertain]
multi_tenancy_model: Process per scenario, as with SUMO; would need Windows workers. Not viable for hosting
build_complexity: High: no source found to build, and a 2013 Windows binary is hard to containerise on Linux servers
scenario_editability: Same as SUMO 2013 XML inputs plus strip-width settings [uncertain]
emissions_support: Inherits SUMO HBEFA-based emissions of its base version [uncertain]
reuse_mode: Inspiration only: reuse the modelling idea and its published validation, not the code. The idea maps directly onto modern SUMO's sublane model (--lateral-resolution ≈ strip width, vType width ≈ strip occupancy)
effort_within_72_hours: Adopting the binary: not feasible (Windows-only 2013 build, no source, obsolete TraCI). Adopting the idea: about 1-2 hours. Set SUMO --lateral-resolution to a strip width of about 0.5-0.8 m, define Indian vTypes with realistic widths, and run a sanity test that throughput rises as resolution narrows and that resolution = lane width matches lane-based results. Cut: porting SiMTraM's custom leader logic and its calibrated parameters unless the paper full text is obtained
licence_constraint: GPLv3: linking or redistributing its code would force GPLv3 on derived distributed code. Moot in practice because no source was found and we will not reuse its code. Reimplementing the published idea carries no licence obligation
known_limitations: Strip discretisation restricts lateral positions to strip multiples. Remains bounded by lane geometry. Abstracts state no quantitative error. Only midblock validation is clear. Single site (Mumbai). Software frozen at a 2013 SUMO base and binary-only, so results are not reproducible today
documented_failures: No documented runtime failures found. The practical failure is staleness: research code was released once as a Windows binary and never maintained or upstreamed into SUMO, so its value survived only as a paper while SUMO independently added a similar sublane model (SL2015) [uncertain]
validation_approach: Calibration of the strip-change parameter on observed strip changes, validation against Mumbai Eastern Express Highway video data, plus a consistency check that strip width equal to lane width reproduces lane-based throughput
takeaway_for_our_build: Lateral discretisation (strips or sublanes) is the proven, cheap way to get Indian mixed traffic in a lane-based engine. Use SUMO's maintained sublane model instead of a fork. Keep the SiMTraM sanity test (resolution = lane width must reproduce lane-based output; finer resolution should raise throughput) as an automated regression check. Never fork the engine core inside a 72-hour build: forks rot, as SiMTraM did
